title: Let me see You
hook: Musa asks to see Allah, the mountain crumbles, and he falls fainting, then repents (7:143)
carry: the mountain could not bear it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Shu'ayb and the scales. Your line was full measure. Where did you give a little more than owed? Today surah seven reaches Musa, and a request nobody expects. Day four hundred twelve.

Musa has been called from beside a fire, has stood before Pharaoh, has watched the sea split. Now Allah sets him an appointment: thirty nights on the mountain, completed with ten more, forty in all. He goes up alone. And there, Allah speaks to him. That's why Muslims give Musa the title kalimullah, the one Allah spoke to. That might seem like enough. Musa, standing in that conversation, asks for one thing more.
screen: `FORTY NIGHTS ON THE MOUNTAIN.` → `KALIMULLAH — THE ONE ALLAH SPOKE TO.` → `ONE THING MORE.`

segments.voice: Verse one-forty-three. Musa says: rabbi arini anzur ilayk. My Lord, show me, so that I may look at You. It's a request made out of longing, not arrogance. And the answer comes, in Pickthall's words: “Thou wilt not see Me, but gaze upon the mountain!” If it stays firm in its place, then you will see Me. Then Allah reveals His glory to the mountain, and the mountain is crushed, made level, turned to dust. And Musa falls down unconscious. When he comes to, his first words are: glory be to You. I turn to You in repentance, and I am the first of the believers. Notice what he repents of. Some commentators say it wasn't a sin, exactly, but asking for more than a human being can bear. The text doesn't scold the longing. It shows its size by showing a mountain that couldn't hold it. Jews and Christians know a related scene in Exodus, where Moses asks to see God's glory and is told no one can see God's face and live. Each tradition tells it in its own way. And the swoon at the mountain echoes later. A hadith in Bukhari says that on the Day of Resurrection, when people fall unconscious, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ will be the first to wake, and he'll find Musa already there, holding the side of the Throne. The Prophet said he didn't know whether Musa woke first, or was spared that swoon because of the one he'd already had on the mountain. Musa's longing, it seems, wasn't wasted.
screen: `MY LORD, SHOW ME.` · `LOOK AT THE MOUNTAIN.` · `CRUSHED TO DUST; MUSA FALLS.` · `GLORY TO YOU; I TURN TO YOU.` · then, large: `THE MOUNTAIN COULD NOT BEAR IT.`

segments.voice: If you can, go stand under something vast: a big sky, a tall tree, a building that makes you tip your head back, even a ceiling in a large room. If you can't move, picture one. Look up. Notice your size next to it. Then remember the mountain in the story, far larger than you, unable to bear a glimpse of the glory. Let the smallness feel safe, not crushing. The bell holds the time.
Let me see You. Musa's request on the mountain, answered with a crumbling peak, a swoon, and glory to You. Today's word.
Your line: the mountain could not bear it. Today, when something makes you feel small, let it bring back the mountain, and the longing that climbed it. Day four hundred twelve.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Musa as kalimullah, the one Allah spoke to; the scene at the mountain is often recited and taught as a picture of longing for God, and of His majesty beyond what creation can bear.

fork.setup: you're Musa. you've asked to see Allah, and you've just woken after the mountain crumbled. what do you say first?
options: glory be to You; I turn to You in repentance.
fork.reveal: glory be to You. I turn to You, and I am the first of the believers. some commentators say he repents of asking for more than a person can bear.

original.note: Arabic: my Lord, show me, that I may look at You (7:143).

trapdoor: what you thought: Musa wanted proof.
what it means: Musa longed to see his Lord, and was shown a mountain that couldn't bear a glimpse of the glory.
what a scholar hears: lan tarani, you will not see Me, is central to the ru'yah debate; Ash'aris read lan as this-world only, Mu'tazilis as never.

Reviewer softening: what Musa repented of is read differently by commentators (asking without permission, asking for what is not given in this world, or simply returning to Allah in awe); the teach and fork reveal now attribute the 'not a sin, exactly' reading to many commentators. Confirm.

Editor review (2026-10-01): 'burning bush' (biblical wording) replaced with the Qur'an's fire (20:10; 28:29–30); cut the superlative 'boldest request in the book' and 'most people would be content'; 'many commentators' softened to 'some'; practice no longer tells the listener what they feel; carry no longer asserts God's greatness in the narrator's voice. The 'spared because of the swoon at the mountain' wording is in Bukhari 2412/3398 rather than 2411; confirm.
